analysis.evidence: יֻלַּד שְׁנֵי בָנִים says that two sons were born to Eber. The verse names them Peleg and Joktan.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and.” The preposition לְ marks Eber, a personal name, as the father to whom the sons were born.
analysis.sense: Eber, the ancestor whose descendants are named here

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68117:1, 66586:3.
analysis.morphology: Pual perfect, third person masculine singular, used impersonally.

analysis.evidence: שְׁנֵי בָנִים counts the two sons born to Eber. The verse names one Peleg and his brother Joktan.
analysis.morphology: Masculine dual construct form of the cardinal numeral, agreeing with בָנִים.

draft.change: Correct the existing Genesis 4:21 evidence note for the identifying-name sense. Jubal is the brother named in the verse.
draft.definition: The name by which a person is known.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 4:21, אָחִיו identifies the person whose name is given, and יוּבָל gives his name.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם הָאֶחָד means “the name of the one,” and פֶּלֶג supplies the name of that son.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, with הָאֶחָד as its complement.
analysis.sense: name by which someone is known

analysis.evidence: שְׁנֵי בָנִים introduces two sons. שֵׁם הָאֶחָד פֶּלֶג names one of them Peleg, and וְשֵׁם אָחִיו יָקְטָן names his brother Joktan.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes the masculine singular absolute cardinal numeral אֶחָד, used substantivally for one son.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם הָאֶחָד פֶּלֶג means “the name of one was Peleg.” The following clause explains the name through a play on נִפְלְגָה, “was divided,” from the same root.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Peleg, one of Eber’s two sons

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces the reason for the name פֶּלֶג (Peleg). The phrase בְיָמָיו נִפְלְגָה הָאָרֶץ means “in his days the earth was divided,” and נִפְלְגָה echoes the name פֶּלֶג.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew conjunction with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The clause כִּי בְיָמָיו נִפְלְגָה הָאָרֶץ explains Peleg’s name by placing the division of the earth within the span of his life.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ means “in.” The masculine plural construct of יוֹם takes a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Peleg.
analysis.sense: (pl.) days of a life, a reign or an age
